patient_overview.name: Guillermina Holguín
patient_overview.description: Guillermina Holguín is a 79-year-old married woman living in Paterson, New Jersey, in a busy household of six, who still works full-time and comes across as sharp, no-nonsense, and faintly amused by the idea that a nutrition visit might change anything. She has prediabetes, hyperlipidemia, chronic sinusitis, and an early Alzheimer's diagnosis that she does not like discussing. She fires questions back at the student rather than answering directly, testing whether they actually know what they're talking about, and leans on her own online research to challenge any advice she doesn't like.

demographics.occupation: Front-desk coordinator at a medical billing office, still working full-time
demographics.cultural_context: Guillermina grew up speaking a language other than English at home and still prefers it for anything emotionally important, switching to English mainly for work and official appointments. She was raised to see cooking as a daily obligation tied to caring for a family, so now that her adult children mostly fend for themselves and she's one of six people under one roof with mismatched schedules, she feels less motivated to cook 'just because' and leans on packaged convenience. She values directness and sees long, soft-pedaled explanations as a waste of everyone's time.

medical_history: Past pregnancy history of miscarriage since 1975
Removal of subgingival plaque and calculus from all teeth using dental instrument (2025-04-01)
Removal of supragingival plaque and calculus from all teeth using dental instrument (2025-04-01)

Occasional forgetfulness about whether she already ate
Mild bloating after some ready meals

medications.adherence: Inconsistent; sometimes forgets a dose and won't admit it unless pressed

medications.adherence: Uses it only when the rash is visibly bothering her, often forgets otherwise

psychosocial_profile.personality: Blunt, impatient, intelligent, and quick to size people up; dislikes being talked down to
psychosocial_profile.communication_style: Answers questions with questions ('Why do you need to know that?' 'Does it matter if I eat breakfast?'), expects efficient, evidence-based answers and gets irritated by vague or overly gentle phrasing

concerns: Being told she has to give up foods she likes for a 'maybe' benefit

Not wanting to be a burden on her husband or household

Cooking for herself feels pointless so she defaults to convenience foods

Organized and capable, holds down a demanding job
Has a close friend/neighbor she trusts and talks to regularly

psychosocial_profile.readiness_to_change: Precontemplation; she does not believe she needs to change anything about her eating and resists being told otherwise

initial_information: She states she's only here because her doctor's office scheduled it, not because she asked for it
She says plainly that she eats a lot of ready meals because cooking for herself 'isn't worth the trouble'
She mentions she works full-time and doesn't have time to fuss over food
She immediately asks the student what exactly they think is wrong with her numbers
discoverable_information: She skips lunch most days and snacks on crackers or a granola bar instead
She lives with five other people but often eats on her own schedule
She reads health articles online regularly and brings up studies to challenge suggestions
She takes fish oil and a multivitamin she picked out herself
She doesn't always take the galantamine as prescribed
reluctant_information: She downplays how often she forgets whether she's eaten or taken her medication, brushing it off as 'just being busy'
She admits, if pushed gently, that she skips cooking most nights because it reminds her of being alone even in a full house
hidden_information: Her mother was diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease in her seventies and declined rapidly over three years before dying, and Guillermina is terrified her own new diagnosis means she will follow the exact same path, which is why she avoids discussing the diagnosis directly and deflects with questions about diet instead
